forms.label: ている past polite

definitions.gloss: to become attached to; to take to; to warm up to
definitions.explanation: To develop affection and trust toward someone, becoming comfortable in their presence. Most commonly used for animals becoming tame and friendly with a person, or for young children warming up to an adult.

examples.english: This cat warmed up to me right away.

examples.japanese: ⟦{近所|きんじょ}→近所：01318_kinjo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{子|こ}ども⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{私|わたし}→私：02988_watashi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{懐|なつ}いて、⟦{毎日|まいにち}→毎日：00729_mainichi⟧⟦{遊|あそ}び→遊ぶ：00550_asobu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{来|く}る→来る：00254_kuru⟧。
examples.english: The neighborhood kid has taken a liking to me and comes to play every day.

examples.japanese: ⟦{野良猫|のらねこ}→野良猫：14440_noraneko⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧エサ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦あげて→あげる：00546_ageru⟧⟦いたら→いる：00495_iru⟧、⟦だんだん→だんだん：00832_dandan⟧{懐|なつ}いてきて、⟦{今|いま}→今：00945_ima⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{膝|ひざ}→膝：00940_hiza⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{上|うえ}→上：00682_ue⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{乗|の}る→乗る：00511_noru⟧ようになった。
examples.english: I kept feeding a stray cat, and it gradually warmed up to me — now it sits on my lap.

notes:
USAGE:
Primarily used for animals and small children, not for adult-to-adult relationships. The subject is the one becoming attached (the animal or child), and the person they warm up to is marked with ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧.

Pattern: [animal/child]⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧[person]⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{懐|なつ}く

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{猫|ねこ}→猫：02237_neko⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{懐|なつ}く (a cat warms up to someone)
- ⟦{犬|いぬ}→犬：00632_inu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{懐|なつ}く (a dog takes to someone)
- {子|こ}ども⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{懐|なつ}く (a child becomes attached)
- ⟦すぐ→すぐ：00814_sugu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{懐|なつ}く (to warm up quickly)
- ⟦なかなか→なかなか：01547_nakanaka⟧{懐|なつ}かない (to not easily warm up)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{慣|な}れる→慣れる：00870_nareru⟧: to get used to — broader; about becoming accustomed, not necessarily affectionate
- ⟦{甘|あま}える→甘える：06624_amaeru⟧: to act spoiled, to be clingy — the behavior that follows after {懐|なつ}く
